author: Ben Doherty
description:
Nothing done to stop planting weapons on dead Afghans, ADF inspector says, as ‘breakdown of command’ allowed ‘egregious behaviour’

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Some Australian SAS officers knew that soldiers under their command were using “throwdowns” – planting weapons on dead Afghan civilians to portray them as combatants – but did nothing to stop the unlawful practice, a previously unpublished military report has said.

Posted online this week, the executive su
title: Australian SAS officers knew about unlawful ‘throwdowns’ on dead Afghans, report says

author: Joe Hinchliffe
description:
Bush Heritage hopes to buy Wooroora station, which links wet sclerophyll forest and savanna woodland and is home to 12 endangered species

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A majestic tract of land in far north Queensland that links wet tropics world heritage rainforest and contains headwaters that flow to the Great Barrier Reef could be bought and protected by Christmas, after a conservation group raised more than $19m in private donations to buy the cattle station.

Wooroora spans more than 20,000 hectares of largely intact wet sclerophyll forest and savanna woodland on the lands of the Jirrbal people about 100km south-west of Cairns – and borders Bush Heritage’s existing 43,575-hectare Yourka Reserve in
title: ‘Worldwide legacy’: almost $20m raised to protect majestic tract of land in far north Queensland

author: Sam Levin
description:
Keaton Denlay says agents handed him ‘poorly formatted Excel spreadsheet’ and threatened to criminally prosecute him

A California county elections official is speaking out about the Department of Justice’s campaign against purported “voter fraud”, saying federal officials provided him a disorganized list of names filled with inaccuracies – and threatened to criminally prosecute him if he didn’t take action.

Keaton Denlay, the county clerk-recorder for Butte county, a region north of Sacramento, said a federal agent on Friday hand-delivered what appeared to be a printout of a “poorly formatted Excel spreadsheet with missing and jumbled information”. The DoJ claimed the list was of 47 “likely” noncitizens who were unlawfully registered to vote and demanded the county set aside their ballots. But Denlay said the document was riddled with errors and lacking crucial details, and he declined to act on it.
title: California election official says federal agents threatened him over ‘voter fraud’

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

US increasingly seen as a ‘threat’ by Australians

Australia’s immediate neighbours are trusted more than historic allies, according to a new survey AAP reports on, which shows the United States is increasingly considered a “threat”.

That climate is no accident. Hate is monetised and weaponised by algorithmic rage-bait. Extremism is incentivised; nuance is penalised. The most available public figures are the most vulnerable.

So tonight is a little reminder of why reason and research matters, why nuance matters, what’s at risk and what’s at stake and why that matters too.
title: Politics live: Chalmers calls social media a ‘business model for hate’; half of young Australians say US a ‘threat’

author: Neha Gohil and press agency
description:
Anthony Williams is accused of attempting to murder passengers and staff on board a London-bound train last November

A knifeman “caused terror and fear on an unimaginable scale” to passengers when he stabbed 10 people on board a London-bound train, a court has heard.

Anthony Williams, 33, is accused of attempting to murder 10 passengers and staff on board an LNER train on 1 November last year and stabbing four people in the 24 hours before.

Continue reading...
title: Knifeman on LNER train ‘caused terror and fear on unimaginable scale’, court hears

author: Chris Stein
description:
Republicans have condemned the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot, calling it a ploy to split votes

Alaska Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign was behind an effort to recruit a challenger with almost the exact same name as the Republican US senator Dan Sullivan, both of whom will appear on the ballot in next week’s midterm elections, the New York Times reported on Wednesday.

Republicans have condemned the presence in the race of two candidates named Dan Sullivan – one the two-term US senator, the second a retiree living in south-eastern Alaska with scant political experience – calling the newcomer a ploy by Democrats to cost the incumbent re-election by splitting his supporters.

Continue reading...
title: Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign reportedly recruited second Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Reform UK leader ‘shocked’ by £10bn pledged to Ukraine and doubles down on cutting tax for crypto investors

  • Budget 2026: key points at a glance

Nigel Farage skipped the chancellor’s first budget because he was worried he would get in a “physical altercation” with another MP in a row over seating arrangements.

The Reform UK leader admitted he was not present in the House of Commons but gave a press conference afterwards in which he said he was “shocked” by the £10bn going to support Ukraine and doubled down on his party’s policies on cutting tax for crypto investors.

Cont
title: Nigel Farage skips budget in Commons over seating ‘altercation’ concerns

author: Associated Press
description:
Effort to loosen rules on unproven peptide drugs, favored by RFK Jr, faced fierce pushback from agency scientists

A plan to give people in the United States easier access to unproven peptide drugs favored by the US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, was opposed by most Food and Drug Administration scientific staff members, who had limited input in drafting the policy, according to six people familiar with its development.

The document posted online on Wednesday by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy.

Continue reading...
title: FDA scientists opposed Trump administration’s move to ease peptide access

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
James O’Keefe and Cam Higby were trying to show vulnerabilities in allowing a voter to vouch for another

Two rightwing influencers have been charged with felonies in Minneapolis over attempts in the state’s election primary to disguise themselves in what they called “Muslim garb” and claim they were local voters.

James O’Keefe and Cam Higby went to polling places in Minnesota during the state’s August primary in an attempt to show vulnerabilities in the practice of “vouching”, where a registered voter from the same precinct can vouch for another voter’s eligibility.

Continue reading...
title: Conservative influencers charged with unlawful voting, disguising themselves in ‘Muslim garb’

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Research looked at prevalence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy in 2,362 players who died in 2008-2023

A new study published on Wednesday estimates that about 75% of former NFL players who died over a 15-year period had evidence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).

The research, published in Jama Network Open and conducted by a Boston-based team, examined the estimated prevalence of the degenerative brain disease among NFL players who died from 2008 through 2023. Researchers found that the estimated rate of CTE among these players was substantially higher than the rates observed in brain samples collected from the general population.

Continue reading...
title: New study estimates 75% of deceased ex-NFL players had brain disease CTE

author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
description:
Mohamed Amersi is suing over Panorama episode that made claims of his suspected involvement in corruption

A Conservative and Reform UK donor lost out on a knighthood and a peerage amid claims of his involvement in corruption, the high court has heard at the start of his defamation case against the BBC.

An episode of Panorama in 2021 and a BBC article caused “very serious harm” to Mohamed Amersi, his barrister, Oliver Powell, said on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
title: BBC allegations cost Tory and Reform donor a peerage, defamation trial told

title: Budget 2026 calculator: find out if you are better or worse off

author: Maya Yang
description:
Twin brothers, 22, from Ghana and a 53-year-old American woman targeted older adults in 25 US states, officials say

Three people have pleaded guilty in a $9m romance fraud scam that targeted elderly Americans.

On Monday, the US attorney’s office in the northern district of Ohio announced that twin brothers from Ghana and an American woman pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

Continue reading...
title: Three plead guilty in $9m romance fraud scam targeting elderly Americans

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Huerta co-founded United Farm Workers union with Cesar Chavez, improving pay and conditions for farm workers

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

Dolores Huerta, a celebrated 1960s labor union leader and civil rights activist, died on Wednesday in California at the age of 96, her family said.

Huerta was co-founder with Cesar Chavez, another veteran unionist and political activist, of the United Farm Workers union (UFW), which was credited with improving pay and conditions for agricultural workers through a series of strikes, boycotts and protests in the 1960s and 1970s.
title: Dolores Huerta, California labor leader and civil rights champion, dies aged 96

author: Mary Jo Pitzl in Scottsdale, Arizona
description:
Circumstances are ripe for change in this onetime Republican stronghold given the current dissatisfaction with Trump agenda, experts say

Donald Trump has repeatedly asked voters to pretend that he is on the ballot in November’s crucial midterm elections. And in the comfortable confines of Arizona’s most affluent and fiercely contested congressional district, Trump is definitely on voters’ minds.

But whether that helps or hurts the warring congressional candidates in this sun-drenched swath of suburbia, where Teslas and walled-in luxury homes dominate, depends on who you ask.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A revolution in slow motion’: is Arizona’s wealthiest district finally done with Trump?

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
The luxury MV Odyssey ship slated for a years-long voyage around the world suspends operations amid high fuel prices

A luxury cruise ship that had embarked on a years-long voyage around the world was forced to suspend its operations and leave passengers stranded in Cambodia because of high fuel prices.

The ship, known as the MV Odyssey, had been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, Cambodian officials told the Associated Press. The ship has a 650-passenger capacity.

Continue reading...
title: Passengers stranded in Cambodia after cruise halted due to high fuel costs

author: Barry Yeoman
description:
Democrats urge FTC to tackle ‘systemic failure’ of biggest convenience and dollar stores over pricing practices after Guardian investigations

Thirty-four members of Congress are calling on the Federal Trade Commission to investigate reports of widespread overcharging by some of America’s most-recognized brand-name retailers.

The 28 October letter to the FTC comes in direct response to Guardian investigations of four of the nation’s largest dollar-store and convenience-store chains. Both investigations revealed pervasive mismatches between shelf labels and register prices.

Continue reading...
title: US lawmakers demand action on overcharging at 7-Eleven, Dollar General and other chains

description:

  • Budget 2026 live – latest updates

Britain’s economy has taken a multibillion-pound hit as the war in the Middle East drags down growth and triggers a fresh cost of living crisis, according to the government’s independent forecaster.

In a report as John Healey announced his first budget, the Office for Budget Respo
title: UK growth forecast for 2027 slashed despite Healey’s budget measures

author: Lisa Cox Environment and climate correspondent
description:
NSW government imposes water restrictions after Menindee water volumes fall below 2021 levels

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Water levels at Menindee Lakes in western New South Wales have fallen to their lowest point in five years, prompting the state government to impose upstream water use restrictions as experts warn of potential mass fish deaths over summer.

Combined storage at Menindee Lakes fell below 480 gigalitres earlier this month, the first time since 2021.

Continue reading...
title: Menindee Lakes water levels drop to lowest in five years as experts warn of mass fish deaths

author: Associated Press
description:
‘You try to leave, it is death,’ Halima Salman testified. Her mother and defense attorneys wept after the verdict

A New York woman whose father took her to Syria as a teenager and arranged her marriage to an Islamic State fighter was convicted on Tuesday of receiving weapons training from the militant group.

Prosecutors said Halima Salman, a US citizen, pledged loyalty to the extremist group and willingly participated in its activities. Jurors were shown a video of her holding an assault rifle, a photo of her with the group’s flag and loving text messages she sent her husband.

Continue reading...
title: US teen whose father arranged her marriage to Islamic State fighter convicted for weapons training

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
EHRC says we need transparency if workers suspect other staff are being paid more for similar work

Workers should have a legal right to know their colleagues’ pay to help prevent pay discrimination, particularly against women, the UK’s human rights watchdog has said.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) made the recommendation in response to government proposals to overhaul equal pay laws, saying workers deserve a right to transparency if they suspect other staff are being paid more for similar work.

Continue reading...
title: Give UK workers right to know colleagues’ pay to prevent disparities, says watchdog

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
US health secretary falsely claims at Mike Rogers rally that Arabs have never won major prizes in science or literature

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, faced backlash on Wednesday for a “wildly racist tirade” during a campaign stop in Michigan in which he falsely asserted that Arabs never won major awards in science or literature.

Kennedy was speaking at the Monday night event in Grand Rapids in support of Mike Rogers, the Republican US Senate candidate who is trailing his Democratic midterms opponent Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim, in polling.

Continue reading...
title: RFK Jr assailed over ‘wildly racist tirade’ about Arabs at Michigan campaign stop

author: Narelle Towie in Perth
description:
As USS Colorado showcases the program in Perth, Peter Briggs says personnel is just one of the ‘huge issues’ it faces

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia faces an uphill battle to recruit and train enough naval personnel to serve on submarines planned for the future fleet of nuclear-powered vessels under the controversial $368bn Aukus deal, a retired admiral has warned.

As the Virginia-class submarine USS Colorado arrived at HMAS Stirling south of Perth on Tuesday for a month of routine maintenance and to help build Australian expertise, retired admiral Peter Briggs said more people needed to be en
title: Australia must recruit hundreds more to crew Aukus submarines, retired admiral warns

author: Eric Berger
description:
Increase will add strain on healthcare system already struggling amid cuts by Trump administration, experts say

The number of people with dementia in the United States is projected to increase dramatically over the next 25 years, which will place increasing strain on a healthcare system already struggling to help them amid cuts by the Trump administration, experts say.

According to a new study in Jama Neurology, the annual incidence of new dementia cases globally will more than double, from 11.4m in 2023 to 24.7m in 2050. In the United States, the number of adults diagnosed with dementia each year will increase from 514,000 in 2020 to 1m by 2060, according to a Jama study published in 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Dementia cases in US projected to rise dramatically by 2050, study finds

description:
Department of Justice says it intends to appeal as administration tries to keep president’s ally Bill Essayli in office

The US Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday during its last rate-setting meeting before the midterm elections, keeping rates at one of the highest pre-election levels seen in over 20 years.

Last month, Fed officials raised rates for the first time since 2023, citing rising inflation. Inflation has hovered for years above the Fed’s target rate of 2%, and for most of this year, the annualized inflat
title: Judge rules Trump-appointed US prosecutor in Los Angeles is not serving legally – US politics live

author: Martin Belam
description:
Benjamin Netanyahu vows to form new coalition while opposition bloc leader says result shows prime minister should step down. Plus, a scathing review of Elon Musk’s AI-generated version of The Odyssey

Good morning. Israel could be in for weeks of political haggling after exit polls and partial official results showed neither Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition nor the opposition bloc led by the former general Gadi Eisenkot had won enough seats to form a government.

With 70% of the vote, or 4m ballots, counted so far, the Netanyahu bloc had 54 seats, the Eisenkot-led Change bloc 47 seats, and the Palestinian parties 19 seats. Sixty-one seats are needed for a majority.

What have the two leaders said so far? Israel’s longest-serving prime minister vowed to assemble a coalition through agreements between his Likud party, far-r
title: Both blocs claim upper hand in crucial Israeli election | First Thing

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Mexican police had said they found Shayna Feinman in Tijuana, raising the hopes of missing Arizonan’s family

Arizona authorities say their Mexican counterparts were resoundingly mistaken when they publicly claimed recently that they found alive a woman who was feared slain after disappearing in 2024 – a turn of events that her sister has called “turmoil” and “heartbreaking”.

The case in question centers on Shayna Feinman, who was reported missing in rural Yavapai county, Arizona, in March 2024 at age 38.

Continue reading...
title: A US woman feared dead was reported alive in Mexico. But cops now say that isn’t true

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
US central bank last month raised rates for first time since 2023, in move that infuriated Donald Trump

The US Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday during its last rate-setting meeting before the midterm elections, keeping rates at one of the highest pre-election levels seen in over 20 years.

Last month, Fed officials raised rates for the first time since 2023, citing rising inflation. Inflation has hovered for years above the Fed’s target rate of 2%, and for most of this year, the annualized inflation rate has remained above 3%.

Continue reading...
title: Fed set to hold interest rates steady in last decision before midterms

author: Julia Kollewe and Anna Isaac
description:
Chancellor’s predecessor Rachel Reeves had planned to reduce allowance from £20,000 to £12,000 a year from April

  • Business live – latest updates

  • What to expect from the budget: who wins, who pays?

John Healey is to use his first budget to ditch plans to slash the annual cash Isa allowance, the Guardian understands, preferring a carrot rather than a stick to encourage people to invest more in shares.

City experts welcomed news that the chancellor will overturn a decision by his predecessor, Rachel Reeves, to cut the allowance from £20,000 to £12,000 a year from
title: Healey poised to overturn cut to cash Isa allowance in first budget

description:
Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo

Local government spokesperson told TVE that the death toll “will almost certainly rise.”

Esther Padilla told the broadcaster the situation “is going to worsen.”

Continue reading...
title: Ten reported dead after two trains collide in Spain – latest updates

author: Sarah Johnson
description:
Jean Kaseya, of the Africa CDC, warns of the illness spreading like Covid unless more funding is secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment

The “unprecedented” spread of the Ebola outbreak means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials.

As the current outbreak reached 10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths, Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.
title: Africa’s ‘unprecedented’ Ebola outbreak could reach UK, says top health official

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
As budget looms, chancellor says he will ask Ofgem to remove ‘unfair and outdated’ fixed daily fee in 2027 or soon after

  • Business live – latest updates

John Healey is abolishing standing charges on gas bills for 23m homes in a move he says will end an “unfair and outdated” practice and save two-thirds of households an average of £45 a year.

Ahead of his first budget statement in the Commons later on Wednesday, the chancellor said he would ask Ofgem, the energy regulator for Great Britain, to remove these charges – which are £108 a year for the typical household – next year or as soon as possible after.
title: John Healey to end standing charges on gas bills for 23m homes

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: First Edition readers and people struggling with the cost of living tell us what the government could do to improve their lives

Good morning. Don’t expect anything radical. This, the Treasury has been at pains to tell us, will be a very “low-key” budget. After weeks of speculation from journalists, a flurry of press releases from thinktanks, and a photoshoot with an obligatory red box, the chancellor, John Healey, will announce the details of the Burnham government’s first budget in the Commons today at 12:30pm.

Healey has been selling this as a series of measures designed to relieve pressure on low- and middle-income households under the mangled tagline of “breathing space for today, fresh hope for the future”. Many of the proposals have already been briefed, and their modesty is a sign of the constraints – both real and self-imposed – that his government faces. He has
title: Wednesday briefing: We asked you - what do you want from the Burnham government’s first budget?

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Tony Blair’s former spokesperson says attacks on UK MPs did not bring about lasting cultural change and overheated rhetoric quickly returned to politics

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Tony Blair’s former communications guru, Alastair Campbell, says the UK political system was too quick to revert to overheated rhetoric and polarisation after attacks on MPs, urging politicians to “re-win the argument for democratic politics”.

More than a week after independent MP Helen Haines was allegedly targeted in an attack outside her electorate office in northern Victoria, c
title: Australia must ‘re-win the argument for democratic politics’ in wake of Haines incident, Alastair Campbell says

description:
Struggling households, new homebuyers and small shops stand to gain, while banks and online marketplaces could face higher levies

John Healey will present his first budget on Wednesday, which will set the tone for Andy Burnham’s premiership.

Despite the chancellor’s promises in the summer that the tax and spending event would not be beset by the leaks that preceded those of his predecessor, Rachel Reeves, both official and unofficial sources have indicated much of what Healey is likely to announce. Here’s what to expect:

title: What to expect from John Healey’s first budget: who wins, who pays?

author: Diane Taylor
description:
Mair Godley claims Essex councillor Carl Johnson told her she was ‘facilitating the invasion’ by giving language lessons

A 78-year-old volunteer has claimed a Reform UK councillor accused her of “facilitating the invasion” and being akin to a Nazi collaborator during the second world war because she has helped asylum seekers learn English.

Mair Godley and her husband, Nick, 77, a former chair of Wethersfield parish council, live near the former Wethersfield military base in Essex, where the Home Office accommodates hundreds of asylum seekers.

Continue reading...
title: Volunteer, 78, says Reform official likened her to Nazi collaborator for teaching asylum seekers English

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
As next week’s all-but certain rate rise looms, there is one thing we can all agree on: the end of war in the Middle East can’t come soon enough

Jim Chalmers is blaming the latest shocking inflation figures on the worsening Middle East conflict, and he has a point.

The trouble is, voters aren’t buying what the treasurer is selling.

Continue reading...
title: Jim Chalmers is blaming Australia’s accelerating inflation on Trump – but voters aren’t buying it

author: Josh Butler
description:
Labor government under pressure to create social media watchdog as new online safety standards bill passes lower house

The federal government wants to ban AI chatbots which seek to create “emotional intimacy” after prime minister Anthony Albanese raised the alarm in a heartfelt speech about children treating these agents as their “best friend”.

But Labor is coming under increasing pressure to empower the telecommunications ombudsman to become a watchdog for social media and AI to give Australians an external complaints mechanism and allow the “naming and shaming” of big tech.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
title: ‘Emotional intimacy’ from AI chatbots would be banned under Australia’s digital duty of care laws

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Talks are aimed at reopening strait of Hormuz and lifting sanctions on Iran, and for Houthis to withdraw in Yemen

A multipronged peace deal to reopen the strait of Hormuz within four days of sanctions being lifted and for the Houthis to withdraw substantial forces inside Yemen are at the heart of Gulf states’ plans to avert what they regard as a disastrous renewal of war between Iran and the US.

The US is aware of the talks’ progress but is holding out for a concession that European powers suggest could involve Iran allowing UN weapons inspectors back into the country.

Continue reading...
title: Gulf states working on multipart peace deal to avert renewal of US-Iran war

author: Benita Kolovos and Henry Belot
description:
Exclusive: ASU launches ‘Ben Lied. Labor lies’ ads while ETU diverts money to defending members at royal commission

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Two major unions in Victoria have turned their back on the Labor government a month out from the state election, with one launching attack ads calling Ben Carroll a liar and the other pulling campaign funding.

The Labor-aligned Australian Services Union (ASU), which launched the ads, has also confirmed it won’t doorknock
title: Two key unions turn on Labor, running attack ads and pulling campaign funds a month out from Victorian election

author: Nino Bucci
description:
Victorian court of appeal to hand down judgment on triple-murderer’s conviction and sentence after her lawyers argued she was denied fair trial

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The decision in Erin Patterson’s appeal against her triple murder conviction will be handed down on Friday, with Victoria’s highest court also set to rule on whether she could face more time in prison.</
title: Erin Patterson to learn fate in appeal against mushroom murders convictions

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
National trust of Victoria award celebrates much-loved arboreal icons while calling for protection of green spaces

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

For more than 160 years, a humble ginkgo tree raised from seed in Geelong’s botanic gardens has been the backdrop to “countless local love stories”. Standing beneath it is the most popular spot to get married at the park, its branches forming the backdrop of many wedding photos.

Now, in addition to being the largest ginkgo biloba in the st
title: ‘Backdrop for countless local love stories’: Geelong gingko named Victorian tree of the year

author: Sara Sneath
description:
Critics warn of climate danger as president in Texas claims change will save companies and consumers billions

Donald Trump announced his administration is “terminating” Biden-era regulations holding oil and gas companies accountable for large leaks of planet-warming methane during a rally in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday evening.

Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save consumers and energy producers $45bn and unlock 210 million barrels of oil – equivalent to about 10 days of US petroleum consumption. “Tonight, I’m officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers,” Trump said, lifting what he called “crippling regulations on methane that caused prices to skyrocket” for small oil and gas operators.

Continue reading...
title: Trump says government to ‘terminate’ Biden-era methane emissions rules

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Naveed Akram, 24, has been charged with 78 offences after allegedly committing a terrorist act. The case has been adjourned until February

  • Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The criminal case against Naveed Akram for his alleged role in the Bondi terror attack faces more delays after an “unprecedented” investigation by the joint counter-terrorism team.

The matter will not return to court until 24 February after it was adjourned on Wednesday before Sydney’s Downing Centre local court. P
title: Criminal case against alleged Bondi terrorist delayed amid ‘unprecedented’ investigation

author: Jonathan Barrett and Patrick Commins
description:
CPI release comes ahead of Reserve Bank decision next week as the Middle East conflict intensifies the cost of living crisis

  • Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s headline inflation rate has accelerated to 4.3%, with a key gauge that strips out volatile prices also elevated, sharpening expectations of another interest rate rise next week.

The Reserve Bank of Australia’s preferred measure of consumer prices, called underlying inflation, came in at an annual 3.6% to September.
title: Australia’s inflation rate rises to 4.3%, fuelling fears of fifth interest rate hike this year

author: Penry Buckley NSW state reporter
description:
Legislation requiring mugs to be offered when people drink at cafes to be scrapped, with environment minister stating ‘we need to clear this up’

  • Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales government has backflipped on its plan to force cafes to offer customers who dine in the option of mugs and glasses instead of takeaway cups.

Chris Minns’ government will also ditch a law that would have required businesses to participate in a reusable cup scheme or risk a fine up to $11
title: ‘I use disposable cups’: Chris Minns backflips on takeaway coffee cups after media and business backlash
